body:
I was trying different python parallelization/jit frameworks like jax and taichi, but I am always coming back to Numba due to it being beginner friendly and one can gradually increase the efficiency with further understanding.
With that being said, I was a bit sad to see that only CUDA was supported as a GPU backend (now it is managed with a [plugin by nvidia](https://github.com/NVIDIA/numba-cuda) themselves) while the support for AMD (ROCm) was first added and then removed.
Supporting all of the platforms would be a huge endeavor for a project like Numba, so a simpler alternative would be great to have.
While exploring taichi I discovered that they support multiple "backends", and one of them were OpenGL/Vulkan. While the multiple backends enabled to write one kernel, which could be executed onto multiple platforms, I was more surprised to see OpenGL/Vulkan support, which meant I was kinda platform agnostic, as long as the target platform could setup/run OpenGL/Vulkan.
Since OpenGL is a bit older, I was wondering how hard it would be to support Vulkan as a backend for Numba.
While the performance would not be on par as using native APIs/frameworks, it would still be a huge benefit and make using different hardware much easier!
There has been a comment regarding using the Vulkan LLVM as an intermediate step for Apples Metal API: https://github.com/numba/numba/issues/5706#issuecomment-985233765

I have no experience in such matters, but if someone could give me some hints where to lookup stuff, I could maybe start with a proof of concept!
title: [Feature request] Vulkan Target
